# Joshos Marine

> Joshos Marine is a marine services business in North Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It does 12V marine electrical work, boat and outboard servicing, boat trailer repairs and custom boat fit-outs for trailer boats. A quote is given before any work starts.

- Service area: North Brisbane, Queensland
- Hours: Mon – Fri 8am – 5pm; Sat – Sun Closed
- ABN: 92 623 093 122
- Book a job online: https://joshosmarine.com.au/#booking
- Website: https://joshosmarine.com.au/

## Services

- [12V marine electrical](https://joshosmarine.com.au/marine-electrical/): Clean, fused and labelled 12V work for trailer boats across North Brisbane, from a single sounder install to a full rewire.
- [Boat & outboard servicing](https://joshosmarine.com.au/boat-servicing/): Routine outboard servicing and the maintenance jobs that keep a trailer boat reliable, for boats across North Brisbane.
- [Boat trailer repairs](https://joshosmarine.com.au/boat-trailer-repairs/): Bearings, brakes, lights and rollers for boat trailers across North Brisbane. It is the part of the rig that gets dunked in salt water every trip.
- [Custom boat fit-outs](https://joshosmarine.com.au/custom-boat-fit-outs/): Boats laid out around the way you fish, dive or cruise, for owners across North Brisbane. Gear goes where it makes sense, and the wiring behind it stays tidy.

## Common questions

### Do I need to know exactly what's wrong before I book?

Not at all. Describe what it's doing, or not doing, and add the make and model if you know them. We'll work out the rest. Photos and short videos help a lot.

### How much will it cost?

It depends on the job, but you'll always get a quote before any work starts. If something unexpected turns up along the way, we'll call you before going any further.

### Can you install gear I've already bought?

Usually, yes. Let us know what it is when you book so we can check it suits your boat and turn up with the right cable, fuses and fittings.

### Which makes and models do you work on?

Most of the common boat, outboard and trailer brands. Put the details in the booking form and we'll confirm before you make the trip.

### How long will the job take?

Smaller installs and most trailer jobs are quick. Full rewires and custom fit-outs take longer. You'll get a realistic timeframe with your quote, and we'll keep you posted if anything changes.

### What area do you cover?

North Brisbane. If you're a bit further out, get in touch and we'll tell you whether we can help.

### Do you come to me?

Depending on the job and where you are, often we can. Tick "come to me" in the booking form and we'll let you know what's possible.

### Can you install electronics I have already bought?

Usually, yes. Tell us the make and model when you book so we can check it suits the boat and turn up with the right cable, fuses and fittings.

### Do I need a second battery?

It depends on what you run. A sounder and a few lights are fine on one battery. Add a fridge, bigger screens or long days at anchor and a separate house battery stops the electronics from flattening the one that starts the motor. Tell us what you run and we will tell you straight.

### Should the old wiring be repaired or replaced?

If the cable is sound and the problem is a few bad joins, a repair is fine. If the cable has gone black inside the insulation, or years of add-ons have no fusing, a rewire usually costs less than chasing faults one at a time. We will tell you which way we would go, and why, before any work starts.

### How long does an install take?

A single sounder or a set of lights is a short job. A dual-battery system or a full rewire takes longer. You will get a realistic timeframe with your quote.

### How often should an outboard be serviced?

Most manufacturers say every 100 hours or once a year, whichever comes first. Boats used in salt water, or left sitting for long stretches, do best on the yearly service even when the hours are low. Your owner's manual has the schedule for your motor.

### Which outboards do you service?

Most of the common brands. Put the make, model and year in the booking form and we will confirm before you book it in.

### What should I tell you when I book?

The make, model and year of the motor, roughly how many hours it has done, when it was last serviced and anything it has been doing that seems off. Photos or a short video help a lot.

### Can you check the trailer at the same time?

Yes. Bearings, brakes and lights can be checked in the same booking, and it usually makes sense to do both together.

### How often should boat trailer bearings be serviced?

As a rule of thumb, once a year for a trailer that goes in salt water, and sooner if a seal has let water in. A warm hub, grease on the wheel or any rumbling means it needs looking at now, not at the next service.

### Does the boat have to come off the trailer?

For most jobs, no. Bearings, brakes, lights and couplings can be done with the boat on. Roller and bunk work can need the boat off, and we will tell you when you book.

### My trailer lights keep failing. Is it the lights or the wiring?

Often both. Bulb-type lights let water in and corrode, and old joins along the frame break down in salt. We test what is there first and quote from that. A sealed LED set and a proper rewire is usually the lasting fix.

### Can you look at the trailer while the boat is booked in for something else?

Yes. It usually makes sense to check bearings, brakes and lights in the same booking as a service or an install.

### Can I supply my own gear?

Usually, yes. Tell us what you have when you book so we can check it suits the boat and plan around it.

### Do you do the electrical side as well?

Yes. Fit-outs and 12V work go hand in hand, so screens, lights, pumps and electric motors are wired as part of the same job.

### How do we work out the layout?

Start by telling us how you use the boat and what annoys you about it now. Photos help. From there we talk through the options and put a quote together before anything is drilled.

### How long does a fit-out take?

It depends on how much is involved. A few rod holders and a bait board is quick. A full deck and console rework takes longer. You will get a realistic timeframe with your quote.
